item.text: The main remaining design leak is traversal state: the solver still owns raw `boolean[] visited` bookkeeping and passes it into DFS helpers. I’m moving traversal state behind a graph-specific traversal object so the algorithm reads at the level of SCC orchestration instead of array management.
The solver now delegates visitation state to a traversal object. I’m compiling and running the sample next, then I’ll check whether the new boundary lets me simplify anything else cheaply.

Refactored the traversal layer so visitation state is no longer leaked into the SCC algorithm.

The main change is [GraphTraversal.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/030_strongly_connected_components/GraphTraversal.java:1), which now owns DFS state and exposes higher-level operations like `buildFinishingOrder()` and `collectReachableVerticesFrom(...)`. That lets [KosarajuStronglyConnectedComponentsFinder.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/030_strongly_connected_components/KosarajuStronglyConnectedComponentsFinder.java:1) focus on Kosaraju orchestration instead of managing raw `boolean[] visited` arrays and threading that state through helper calls. I removed the old [DepthFirstTraversal.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/030_strongly_connected_components/DepthFirstTraversal.java:1) in favor of this graph-bound traversal object.
